what_its_for: Mannitol is used for several purposes depending on how it is given. When given through an IV (into your vein) in a hospital, it helps reduce dangerous swelling in the brain or around the eyes, and helps your kidneys produce more urine to remove excess fluid from your body. When inhaled as a powder (Bronchitol/Aridol), it helps clear thick mucus from the airways in people with cystic fibrosis or is used to test for asthma. Your doctor has prescribed this medicine to help manage one of these conditions.
how_to_take: Mannitol is almost always given by a healthcare provider in a hospital or clinic setting. The IV form is given directly into your vein through a drip (infusion). If you are using the inhaled powder form (Bronchitol) at home, breathe it in through a special inhaler device as shown to you by your doctor or nurse. Always follow the exact instructions given to you by your healthcare team. Do not try to give yourself the IV form at home unless specifically trained and instructed to do so.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose based on your weight, medical condition, kidney function, and how your body responds to treatment. For the IV form given in the hospital, doses are calculated carefully by the medical team. For the inhaled form (Bronchitol), the usual adult dose is 400 mg (10 capsules) inhaled twice daily, about 12 hours apart. Never change your dose on your own. Always follow what your doctor tells you.
missed_dose: For the inhaled form at home: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. For the IV form given in the hospital, your healthcare team will manage your dosing, so you do not need to worry about missing a dose.
storage: Store the inhaled capsule form (Bronchitol) at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it in a dry place away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Keep the capsules inside their original packaging until you are ready to use them. Do not store capsules inside the inhaler device. Keep all forms of mannitol out of reach of children. The IV form is stored and handled only by hospital staff.
what_to_avoid: Avoid becoming dehydrated while taking mannitol, as this can make side effects worse. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or confused, as these can be side effects of mannitol. Avoid alcohol, as it can worsen dizziness and dehydration. If using the inhaled form, avoid using it if you have had a recent lung infection or if your breathing suddenly gets much worse — contact your doctor first. Do not swallow the inhaled capsules; they are for inhalation only.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek emergency medical help right away if you experience: sudden shortness of breath or severe wheezing after inhaling mannitol, chest pain or tightness, signs of a severe allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing, severe headache, vision changes, or confusion, decreased urination or no urination at all, signs of too much fluid loss such as extreme thirst, dry mouth, dizziness, or rapid heartbeat, muscle weakness, cramps, or irregular heartbeat (signs of electrolyte imbalance), or unusual swelling in your hands, feet, or legs.
when_it_works: For the IV form given in the hospital to reduce brain swelling or increase urine output, mannitol usually begins working within 30 to 60 minutes and its effects can last for 3 to 8 hours. Your medical team will monitor how well it is working during treatment. For the inhaled form used in cystic fibrosis, it may take several weeks of regular use before you notice the best improvement in mucus clearance and breathing. Keep using it every day as directed, even if you feel better.
special_populations: Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of mannitol, especially regarding fluid and electrolyte changes and kidney function. Careful monitoring by a doctor is important. Kidney problems: Mannitol must be used very carefully or avoided in people with severe kidney disease, as it can build up in the body and cause harmful effects. Your doctor will check your kidney function before and during treatment. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using mannitol. The safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established, so your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits carefully. Children: The IV form is used in children in hospital settings under close medical supervision. The inhaled form (Bronchitol) is approved for children 6 years and older with cystic fibrosis; dosing and safety are monitored by the healthcare team.
